subject: Global private offer: tax wiring, rev-share alignment & term exceptions
messages:
From: Lexi Sanders <lexi.sanders@acme-global.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-global.com
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer request: Acme Global - tax/royalty structure

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited to move to a Private Offer on AWS Marketplace. Before we proceed, procurement needs clarity on two items that will affect invoicing across our EU entities:

- Tax wiring: Acme will be withholding VAT at source in some countries; we need to confirm Redwood can accept marketplace invoicing with gross amounts and handle the withholding documentation.
- Rev-share / royalty split: Acme requests a 15% marketplace rev-share carveout with a 30% pass-through to our reseller layer (they want a guaranteed minimum payment schedule).

Attached is the preliminary SOW and the procurement checklist (Acme_PO_SOW.pdf). Can you confirm whether these tax and rev-share structures are acceptable under a private offer and what approvals you need internally?

Best,
Lexi
Lexi Sanders
Head of Procurement — Acme Global

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private offer request: Acme Global - tax/royalty structure

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Acme's ask. Key points and suggested asks for Deal Desk / Exec:

1) Tax wiring: Acme will require marketplace gross-invoice acceptance and will withhold local VAT in a number of EU entities. Procurement wants a Redwood confirmation that we will not be responsible for gross-to-net reconciliation beyond providing standard marketplace tax docs (invoices, W-8/W-9 equivalents).
2) Rev-share: They asked for 15% marketplace rev-share with an internal pass-through arrangement. Our standard private offer rev-share is 12% for this tier; to get the deal done they want 15% and a 30% pass-through guarantee.
3) Payment terms: Acme is pushing Net60 but procurement will accept Net45 if we give a 10% concession to the rev-share split.

What I need from you (fast):
- Can Deal Desk approve an exception to increase marketplace rev-share to 15% and allow the pass-through? If not, what's our maximum concession without VP signoff?
- Can we accept marketplace gross invoicing with tax withholding clauses limited to the local Acme entities, provided Legal signs the amendment?

I'm attaching a short summary with modeled economics (acme_summary.xlsx). Timing: Acme wants to close this week and will escalate to their CFO if we delay.

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer request: Acme Global - tax/royalty structure

Diego — thanks for the heads up and the model. Quick thoughts:

- Rev-share: Deal Desk policy allows up to a 10% rev-share on this tier without VP approval. Anything above 10% requires VP Sales signoff and Finance + Legal signoff for payout mechanics.
- Pass-through / reseller guarantees: we can agree to a pass-through arrangement in contract language but we need precise language about how the pass-through is calculated and whether it creates any clawback exposure for Redwood. Legal will want to see the reseller agreement or the payment flow.
- Tax wiring / gross invoicing: Accepting gross invoices with local withholding is feasible only if Legal confirms our indemnity exposure is limited and Finance confirms we can net to our GL without double-tax risk.

Suggested path:
1) Marissa signs off on up to 10% rev-share as an immediate concession to get to Net45.
2) For any rev-share request >10% (they asked 15%), route to VP for one-off approval; get Legal to draft a limited-scope addendum that caps Redwood's liability on withholding and requires Acme to indemnify for any additional local tax assessments.
3) Finance (Laura) reviews the model and confirms whether Net45 with a 10% rev-share preserves our unit economics.

If you want, I can prepare VP language and a short packet for Marissa to escalate — timebox this to 48 hours.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

---
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 May 2029 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer request: Acme Global - tax/royalty structure

Team — I'm ok to approve a targeted concession to close this quarter, with strict guardrails:

- Approve up to 10% marketplace rev-share in exchange for Net45 payment terms. This is immediate — Diego, tell Acme we can accept Net45 and 10% rev-share.
- Anything >10% rev-share (Acme asked 15%) requires my VP's approval. Karthik, please prepare the VP packet with the economics and suggested approval wording.
- Legal must sign an addendum that does both: (a) limits Redwood's exposure for withholding/tax assessments to providing standard invoices and (b) requires Acme to indemnify for incremental local tax liabilities.
- Finance review required: Laura, please confirm the model in acme_summary.xlsx and indicate whether a temporary 10% concession is acceptable (no permanent changes to list rev-share).

Marcus — I looped you because this will touch marketplace invoicing mechanics and partner flows; if this becomes a multi-reseller pass-through, we need to confirm our payout pipeline can route to the reseller and record the pass-through amounts correctly.

Diego — once Laura confirms finance, I'll sign off and Karthik can escalate to VP if Acme insists on 15%.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 14:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer request: Acme Global - tax/royalty structure

Marissa / Team — Finance reviewed the acme_summary.xlsx and confirmed the following:

- We can accept Net45 with a temporary 10% marketplace rev-share concession for this closed-won activity, provided the concession is documented as a one-off (term sheet or amendment) and does not change our published rates.
- We CANNOT accept structural exposure that leaves Redwood liable for foreign withholding tax assessments. Any contract language must include an explicit Acme indemnity for withholding and require Acme to provide completed local tax receipts within 60 days of invoice.
- If Acme insists on >10% rev-share (their 15% ask), escalate to VP Sales + CFO for approval — Finance would only accept >10% if there is a compensating upfront credit or guaranteed minimum monthly payment that offsets the margin impact.

Next steps:
- Diego: Communicate to Acme that Redwood can do Net45 + 10% rev-share as a one-off and attach a term sheet amendment requiring Acme indemnity for withholdings. 
- Karthik: Prepare the VP packet outlining the economics and propose a compensating structure if Acme presses for 15% (e.g., $250k minimum guarantee or 6-month upfront credit).
- Marcus / Legal: Confirm marketplace payout mechanics and include the reseller pass-through mechanics in the addendum.

I'm attaching a stubbed 'signed' term sheet for routing (signed_term_sheet_stub.pdf) and adding the DocuSign envelope we should use for rapid acceptance: https://www.docusign.net/embeddedSigning/abcdef123456

Laura Bennett
